m2Definition.definition: A current rights-cleared nationwide seven-character Eircode assignment denominator, preserving the D6W Routing Key exception and the fact that each full Eircode is an address/property identity rather than an area, and an authoritative or rights-cleared real Polygon/MultiPolygon release for all 139 Routing Keys are pinned by edition, validity, terms, CRS, SHA-256, coverage and exceptions and published as an approved immutable artifact. Searching a normalized full Eircode through the real IE API/app must return its honest point/non-area reason and, when available, the separately labelled official/derived/virtual Routing Key context surface, fit the map and render translucent fill plus a clear outline with selected code, geometry kind, source, reference date and confidence. Finder markers, ECAF/ECAD fields without publication rights, GISCO/TERCET point or NUTS correspondence, CSO statistical classifications, counties, buildings, parcels, buffers, Voronoi cells and synthetic planning fixtures never satisfy M2.

officialObservations.finding: Eircode states that every seven-character code is unique to a postal address and geographic location. The first three characters are a Routing Key, the last four a Unique Identifier, and 139 postal areas are in use; areas may cross county borders. A full Eircode is therefore not a grouped postcode polygon.

The official FAQ describes monthly and quarterly GeoDirectory updates, public Finder building markers, over 2.2 million assigned postal addresses, optional space formatting and exclusion of the letter O. It says licensed businesses receive data updates and does not grant bulk extraction or area-geometry rights.

ECAF is an address-point file with Eircode and postal address; ECAD adds coordinates and other address-related fields. The current page requires annual purchase/licence and distributes editions and updates through a secure customer portal. No product or contract was obtained.
The legal page protects website/database content and limits sample use; evaluation access does not authorize resale, a derivative database, a public lookup service or unrestricted redistribution.

The PDF linked from the current products page describes one-year Provider and Direct End User licences, internal-use-only restrictions for Direct End Users and Provider rights for resale/integration. Its price schedule says effective March 2015, so it is used only as licence-gate evidence, not as a claim about current prices.

Section 2.2 defines a letter-number-number Routing Key with D6W as the sole letter-number-letter exception and a four-character Unique Identifier. It says 139 postal-town references are in use and assignment is to each complete postal address/property from GeoDirectory source data.

The 11 August 2026 official update says the most recent update is live in Eircode Finder and new-code notification letters were posted. It proves a current Finder refresh, not a reusable bulk edition or area release.

GISCO publishes postal-code point/NUTS correspondence under CC BY-SA 4.0 and warns about location, coverage and non-geographic-code limitations. A point or NUTS match is not an Eircode Routing Key perimeter.

The IE row contains zero member-state postal rows, zero member-state-address rows, 139 GeoNames rows, zero GISCO-2020 carryovers and zero manual rows. The output is extracted without centroids and the methodology warns that location and coverage are imperfect.
The ZIP contains one CSV with only NUTS3 and CODE. It has 139 unique format-valid Routing Keys including D6W across eight NUTS3 codes, and no coordinates or Polygon/MultiPolygon.
The current CSO quality-report index links the 2026 SIMS report used in this audit.

CSO classifies outputs by Eircode Routing Key Areas, but receives ESB data under Section 24, publishes no individual domestic connection and allows no microdata access outside CSO. Point-in-polygon joins are an internal statistical process, not a public Routing Key boundary release.

The current release says splits by Local Authority, Eircode Routing Key and Local Electoral Area use substation information rather than exact dwelling location and may not precisely accord with geographical boundaries. This is not a boundary dataset.

dataQuality.risk: The public official pages establish a current address-level postcode system and 139 Routing Keys, but reusable current assignments and real Routing Key boundaries are licensed or unavailable. The only downloaded list is a GeoNames-derived NUTS crosswalk with no geometry.

blockerSummary: A seven-character Eircode is an address/property identity, not an area. ECAF/ECAD and updates are licensed; no product or agreement was obtained. TERCET lists 139 GeoNames-derived Routing Keys against NUTS3 but has no coordinates or geometry, while CSO uses confidential/internal geospatial processing and publishes no microdata or boundary release. No rights-cleared real IE Routing Key Polygon/MultiPolygon or approved immutable artifact exists.
